progress.title: Failing regressions + test seams
progress.summary: Added minimal non-behavior-changing test seams, then wrote deterministic regression tests that fail against the unfixed baseline for 6 of 7 required defect categories. No production behavior was changed in this phase.
seams_added: sessions/store.rs: pub(crate) trait RecordWriter (acquire_lock/write_pending/write_final/write_terminal_unlocked), implemented for CommandRecordStore, so lifecycle coordination can depend on an abstraction instead of a concrete store.

commands.rs: pub(crate) type StoreFactory (Send + Sync dyn Fn) + default_store_factory, threaded through run_lifecycle_with_executor and persist_terminal, enabling deterministic write-fault injection without relying on filesystem permission bits.
sessions/recovery.rs: pub fn recover_abandoned_pending_with_hook with an optional pre-lock hook, reproducing the finalize-between-read-and-lock race deterministically.
commands.rs test harness: fixed a pre-existing env_lock() mutex-poisoning bug (poison recovery via into_inner()) so a failing fault-injection test no longer cascades into unrelated test failures.

regressions_added.covers: Sec 7.1 audit-write-propagation matrix: Deny/Gate/plan-only/unavailable terminal-install failure (0 executor calls); initial pending failure (0 calls); PID-bearing pending replace failure; terminal replace failure; unavailable-executor terminal replace failure

finalize-between-read-and-lock race; lock acquired for one session writing another session's record; final replace not bound to installed pending plan_digest; terminal->pending regression; terminal->different-terminal transition; list ordering by parsed instant vs lexical started_at string across UTC offsets
Deny+completed, Gate+planned, Allow+denied currently accepted by RuntimeCommandRecord::validate()
session latest drops the skipped-record diagnostics that session list surfaces; an explicit unknown --profile silently falls through to XDG/HOME instead of failing closed
human-mode RTK-eligible asymmetric overflow: stderr over the capture limit causes finalize_output's combined branch to drop the still-buffered under-limit stdout stream entirely

deferred: S6.1-07 (post-spawn controller-failure truth): AuthorizedExecutionPlan is intentionally evaluator-private (S5.2 boundary), and no seam exists to force a post-spawn pipe-take/signal-install failure through the public CLI surface. The addendum's Sec 5.6 already requires adding an injectable signal-source/process adapter as a production correction, so the seam, its failing regression, and the fix will be added together in Phase 3.
S6.1-13 (unsound Cell<u32> + unsafe impl Sync SpyExecutor): a pure soundness correction with no meaningful failing-test shape; will be corrected directly alongside the Phase 3 execution/mod.rs work.

progress.title: Correct the state-transition core (lock binding, legal transitions, under-lock recovery re-read, propagate every coordinator write error)
progress.summary: Fixed S6.1-01, S6.1-02, S6.1-03, S6.1-04, and S6.1-13 in production code. All Phase 1 regressions for these five findings now pass; no new test seams were required beyond Phase 1's.
fixes_applied: sessions/recovery.rs (S6.1-04): SessionLock now carries the session_id it was acquired for, with a session_id() accessor.

sessions/store.rs (S6.1-04): write_pending/write_final now call check_lock_matches_record (a lock only authorizes writing the record for its own session) and write_final additionally calls check_legal_transition, which re-reads the currently installed record and requires it to be a live pending record with the same plan_digest before allowing the replace; a terminal record is immutable except for a byte-identical idempotent retry.

sessions/recovery.rs (S6.1-03): recover_abandoned_pending_with_hook now re-reads the record under the lock it just acquired before finalizing as abandoned, short-circuiting (without writing) if the under-lock read shows the record already went terminal, and failing closed if the session_id/plan_digest identity changed between the pre-lock read and the lock acquisition.

commands.rs (S6.1-01/S6.1-02): replaced every `let _ = persist_terminal(...)` and `let _ = store.write_final(...)` discard with `?`-propagation mapped to ControllerError::StateIo, at all 5 call sites (Deny/Gate terminal install, execution-class-unavailable terminal install, plan-only terminal install, PID-bearing pending replace, execution_unavailable stand-in terminal replace).

execution/mod.rs (S6.1-13): SpyExecutor.calls is now AtomicU32 (fetch_add/load) instead of Cell<u32> with a compensating `unsafe impl Sync`; added a calls() accessor. Updated all call sites in commands.rs and policy/authorize.rs from `.calls.get()` to `.calls()`.

progress.title: Correct execution/stream truth and bound RTK (pre-/post-spawn split, independent per-stream emission, canonical RTK identity/bounded I/O/timeout)
progress.summary: Fixed S6.1-07, S6.1-05, and S6.1-06 in production code. Re-read the full addendum (Sec 5.4-5.6) and process.rs/streams.rs/rtk.rs/signals.rs/mod.rs before changing anything. The one Phase 1 regression scoped to this phase (execution_cli human_mode_rtk_eligible_asymmetric_overflow_drops_under_limit_stream, S6.1-05) now passes; S6.1-06 and S6.1-07 had no pre-existing failing-test seam (S6.1-07 needed a new injectable seam; S6.1-06 needed a new fake-RTK test harness), so their regressions were written directly against the fix and confirmed to exercise the intended mechanism (e.g. the identity-drift test fails with the wrong diagnostic if the revalidation guard is removed).
fixes_applied: execution/process.rs (S6.1-07): added an injectable SignalFactory seam (TokioExecutor::execute now calls execute_inner via default_signal_factory; tests can substitute a failing factory). Added ExecFailure::controller_error (spawned=true, pid preserved, outcome=controller_error) distinct from the pre-spawn failed_to_spawn constructor. Added reap_after_controller_failure (SIGKILLs the process group, disarms the guard, awaits child.wait()) called before reporting a missing stdout pipe, missing stderr pipe, or signal-factory failure. The post-run_capturing wait-failure path now also uses controller_error instead of overwriting an io-outcome failure's spawned/pid fields post hoc, and only disarms the guard on a successful wait (killing the group first on a wait error).

execution/process.rs (S6.1-05): finalize_output's Human branch now calls a new finalize_human_stream helper independently for stdout and stderr instead of one combined branch whose guard clause (both streams eligible, neither truncated, both UTF-8) caused the entire branch — including an unaffected under-limit peer stream — to be skipped whenever either stream overflowed. Added write_human_bytes (per-label stdout/stderr dispatch) and merge_compressor (rtk > unsupported > none precedence) helpers.

output/rtk.rs (S6.1-06): resolve_rtk_binary now requires a canonical, regular, executable file (canonical_rtk_identity) instead of accepting any is_file() candidate. Added adapter_command, which clears the environment, disables telemetry, and puts the adapter in its own process group (setpgid) for both probe and pipe invocations. apply_rtk_if_eligible now revalidates the canonical identity immediately before spawning the pipe (rejecting any drift between probe and pipe as unavailable/rtk_identity_drift, never spawning an unverified binary). pipe_stream now writes stdin and drains stdout/stderr concurrently on three separate threads (fixing the deadlock when the adapter echoes more than one pipe buffer), caps stdout/stderr independently and discards content past the cap while continuing to drain (so an oversized adapter is rejected, not accepted partially, without blocking the adapter), enforces a short default timeout (1.5s) via a try_wait poll loop, and on timeout/wait-failure kills the adapter's process group and reaps it before returning. Stderr remains discarded (never copied into user output or diagnostics).

progress.title: Close query and durable-contract semantics (parsed RFC 3339 ordering, latest diagnostics, strict query-profile resolution, decision/outcome/provenance validation, runtime-context diagnostics)
progress.summary: Fixed S6.1-08, S6.1-09, S6.1-10, and S6.1-11 in production code. Re-read addendum Sec 5.7-5.10, 6, and 7.1-7.7 before changing anything. The 4 Phase-1 regressions scoped to this phase (contracts_roundtrip decision_outcome_semantic_mismatches_are_rejected; session_cli session_list_with_unknown_profile_must_fail_closed and session_latest_drops_skipped_record_diagnostics; session_store list_orders_by_parsed_instant_not_lexical_string_despite_offsets) now pass. S6.1-11 had no pre-existing failing regression, so a new end-to-end CLI test was added directly against the fix.
fixes_applied: registry/types.rs + registry/mod.rs (S6.1-09): added ProfileSelection enum (Explicit/Default/None) and ProfilesDocument::resolve_profile_selection(explicit, env_profile), a single strict CLI-then-env-then-workspace-dev-if-present precedence implementation shared by both call sites instead of two divergent inline implementations.
resolution/profile.rs (S6.1-09): select_profile now delegates to resolve_profile_selection instead of duplicating the precedence logic.

commands.rs (S6.1-09): run_session's profile resolution now calls access.load_profiles()? (was .ok(), silently swallowing a malformed-profiles error) and matches on ProfileSelection: Explicit(id) requires a matching profile or returns ControllerError::usage("unknown profile: {id}"); Default(id) looks up the state home only if that profile exists; None opens no profile. No state directory is opened before profile resolution succeeds.

contracts/timestamp.rs (new, S6.1-08): hand-written strict RFC 3339 parser (parse_rfc3339_utc_seconds) with no external date/time crate dependency, validating calendar/leap-year/day-in-month correctness, fractional seconds, and Z/±HH:MM offsets, normalized to epoch seconds via the same days_from_civil algorithm sessions/store.rs already uses for civil_from_days. 6 unit tests (offset equivalence, lexical-vs-chronological ordering, invalid calendar rejection, malformed/missing-offset rejection, fractional-seconds acceptance).

sessions/query.rs (S6.1-08): load_sorted now parses each record's started_at via parse_rfc3339_utc_seconds, skipping unparseable records with a bounded diagnostic instead of sorting by the raw lexical string; sort compares the parsed instant with session-ID-descending as the deterministic tie-break. Added show_latest_with_diagnostics, returning the same skipped-record diagnostics list as list_sessions; show_latest now delegates to it, discarding diagnostics only for its own backward-compatible callers.

commands.rs (S6.1-08): SessionCommand::Latest now calls show_latest_with_diagnostics and threads the diagnostics into emit_session_record's JSON output (a data.diagnostics array), matching how session list already surfaces skipped-record diagnostics.

contracts/types.rs (S6.1-10): RuntimeCommandRecord::validate() now enforces the addendum's full decision/outcome/provenance mapping: policy_decision must match execution.outcome per the required table (denied->Deny, gated->Gate, pending/planned/execution_unavailable/failed_to_spawn/completed/interrupted/controller_error->Allow; abandoned is unconstrained here since it retains whatever the originating pending record carried); embedded resolution must match schema_version/profile_id/request.unit_id/request.verb+request.command/registry_generation.source_fingerprints (in addition to the pre-existing session_id check); started_at/ended_at must parse as RFC 3339 with ended_at >= started_at; plan_digest must be sha256: plus exactly 64 lowercase hex characters; interrupted records' signal must be one of the four names execution/signals.rs::signal_name can produce; runtime_context opaque IDs must satisfy the same bound/character rules sessions/runtime_context.rs::normalize_id enforces at capture time; error.code is now bounded (1-128 bytes) alongside the pre-existing error.message 4 KiB bound.

contracts_roundtrip.rs: updated bounded_child_output_and_terminal_outcomes to pass a matching Deny/Gate decision for the denied/gated positive fixtures (previously all outcomes shared one Allow default, which is now correctly rejected for denied/gated by the tightened validate()).

session_store.rs: fixed a latent test-fixture bug in list_limit_bounds_and_default (ended_at was a fixed timestamp earlier than most generated started_at values), now caught by the new ended_at >= started_at check.

commands.rs + output/mod.rs (S6.1-11): collect_runtime_context's diagnostic is no longer discarded with `_`. Collected once per invocation and threaded through base_record_from_authorized/base_record_from_rejected: the durable record's error field receives the runtime-context diagnostic whenever nothing more severe has been recorded yet (a later execution diagnostic, if any, still overwrites it -- the addendum's 'preserve the more severe execution cause' rule falls out naturally from write order). Independently, the same diagnostic is now threaded as a new extra_diagnostics parameter into emit_plan_with_policy, emit_explanation_with_policy, emit_policy_outcome, emit_error_with_explanation, and emit_executed, appended to each envelope's existing diagnostics list (and printed on stderr in human mode) so it is surfaced even for Deny/Gate records whose error field is already the policy diagnostic.

progress.title: Close E09_DEFERRED.md D2 (remaining §7.1-7.7 matrix gaps)
progress.summary: Closed every remaining 'still open' row in E09_DEFERRED.md's §7 coverage map: §7.2 concurrent distinct-session writers + malformed under-lock record; §7.3 full positive outcome set (both pending shapes); §7.4 malformed profiles document + missing workspace-dev default; §7.5 SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP forwarding, second-signal SIGKILL escalation, descendant process-group cleanup, executable/permission/cwd-drift preflight rejection, missing-pipe and wait-failure error-shape construction, reader failure; §7.6 raw-stream edge table (empty/no-newline/exact-limit/one-byte-over/invalid-utf8/binary), UTF-8 split across reads, one-stream-closes-early, and both broken-pipe directions. §7.2/7.4 were delegated to two background subagents scoped to disjoint files (session_cli.rs; contracts_roundtrip.rs) to avoid file conflicts; §7.5/7.6 and the remaining §7.3 gap were done directly. This run also found and fixed one genuine production bug (not just a coverage gap): output/mod.rs::emit_executed's human-mode diagnostic echo used `writeln!(io::stderr(), ...)?`, so a broken pipe on the controller's own stderr while echoing diagnostics propagated as a `ControllerError::internal` (exit code 1, INTERNAL) even when the child had already truly completed with exit 0 -- the persisted record was correct but the process's own exit code lied about the outcome. Fixed by swallowing a broken-pipe write there (matching the swallow-broken-pipe philosophy already used everywhere else in the output/stream code), proven by stderr_broken_pipe_still_captures_writable_stdout, which failed with this exact exit-code mismatch before the fix.
fixes_applied: output/mod.rs: added is_broken_pipe() helper; emit_executed's human-mode diagnostic-echo loop now checks each writeln! result and only propagates a non-broken-pipe io::Error, instead of letting `?` unconditionally overturn an already-decided exit code.

execution/process.rs: extracted missing_pipe_failure(pid, label) and wait_failure(err, pid) as small pure functions (previously inlined ExecFailure::controller_error(...) calls) so the exact error-shape construction for two Tokio-unreachable-in-practice conditions is directly unit-testable; added #[derive(Debug)] to ExecFailure to support .expect() in the new preflight_identity tests.
